To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the accuracy of children's perceptions of asthma and diabetes symptoms and their ability to use this information to guide their self-management behaviors are related to the accuracy with which they perceive their symptoms, the severity of their disease, and the extent of their experience with the disease.

(1) perceptual accuracy is the degree to which a child accurately perceives his or her own health condition and its severity, and (2) perceptual accuracy can be measured and is associated with health outcomes in pediatric asthma and pediatric diabetes.

the accuracy with which children with type 1 diabetes or asthma perceive the severity of their symptoms is associated with their disease control, and that the accuracy of symptom perception is influenced by their cognitive and social skills and by their beliefs about their illness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of novel, innovative methods for measuring perceptual accuracy in asthma and diabetes.
